questions.q: Simplify the ratio $18:24$ to lowest terms.
Solve the proportion $\frac{5}{8}=\frac{x}{40}$.
A recipe requires flour and sugar in the ratio $3:2$. If 12 cups of flour are used, how much sugar is needed?
If $a:b=4:7$ and $b=35$, find $a$.
A car uses 8 gallons of gas to travel 224 miles. Find its fuel efficiency in miles per gallon.
A printer produces 150 pages in 6 minutes. Find its rate in pages per minute, and use it to find how long it takes to print 400 pages.
questions.answer: Rate $=\frac{150}{6}=25$ pages per minute. Time $=\frac{400}{25}=16$ minutes.
questions.explanation: Rate $=\frac{150}{6}=25$ pages per minute. Time $=\frac{400}{25}=16$ minutes.

sections.heading: Part II — Free-Response Questions (FRQs): Intermediate Multi-Step Application (8–14)

questions.q: A jacket originally 120 dollars is discounted 30 percent. Find the sale price.
A population decreases by 15 percent one year, then increases by 15 percent the next. Is the final population the same as the original?
questions.answer: Start with 100. After a 15\% decrease: $85$. After a 15\% increase: $85\times1.15=97.75$. No — the final population is 2.25\% less than the original.
questions.explanation: Start with 100. After a 15\% decrease: $85$. After a 15\% increase: $85\times1.15=97.75$. No — the final population is 2.25\% less than the original.

questions.q: An investment of 2000 dollars grows to 2300 dollars after one year. Find the percentage increase.
A student scores 80 on a test worth 40 percent of the grade and 90 on a test worth 60 percent of the grade. Find the weighted average grade.
A store sells 3 items at 10 dollars each and 7 items at 20 dollars each. Find the average price per item sold.
questions.answer: Total revenue $=3(10)+7(20)=30+140=170$ dollars. Total items $=10$. Average $=\frac{170}{10}=17$ dollars.
questions.explanation: Total revenue $=3(10)+7(20)=30+140=170$ dollars. Total items $=10$. Average $=\frac{170}{10}=17$ dollars.

sections.heading: Part III — Free-Response Questions (FRQs): Challenging & Cross-Lesson Synthesis (15–20)

questions.q: A table shows the hours worked by 4 employees in a week: A: 32, B: 40, C: 28, D: 36. Find the total hours worked and the mean hours per employee.
A table shows quarterly revenue, in thousands of dollars: Q1: 50, Q2: 65, Q3: 70, Q4: 55. Find the percentage of annual revenue earned in Q3, to the nearest tenth of a percent.
The bar graph shows a company's monthly sales, in thousands of dollars. Find the percentage increase in sales from January to March.
A factory produces 450 units using 6 machines running for 8 hours. Assuming the same rate per machine-hour, how many units would 9 machines produce in 8 hours?
questions.answer: Rate $=\frac{450}{6\times8}=\frac{450}{48}=9.375$ units per machine-hour. New machine-hours $=9\times8=72$. Units $=72\times9.375=675$.
questions.explanation: Rate $=\frac{450}{6\times8}=\frac{450}{48}=9.375$ units per machine-hour. New machine-hours $=9\times8=72$. Units $=72\times9.375=675$.

questions.q: If 5 workers can build a fence in 12 days, how many days would it take 4 workers, assuming the same work rate per worker?
questions.answer: Total work $=5\times12=60$ worker-days. Days for 4 workers $=\frac{60}{4}=15$ days.
questions.explanation: Total work $=5\times12=60$ worker-days. Days for 4 workers $=\frac{60}{4}=15$ days.

questions.q: This question has three parts. In the first quarter, a business had 240 customers, and 180 of them made a repeat purchase. (a) Find the repeat-purchase rate as a percentage. (b) In the second quarter, the number of customers grew by 25 percent, and the repeat-purchase rate held steady at the percentage found in part (a). Find the number of repeat customers in the second quarter. (c) The business sets a goal to raise the repeat-purchase rate to 80 percent by the third quarter, while keeping the same total number of customers as the second quarter. Find how many additional repeat customers (beyond part (b)'s total) are needed to reach this goal.
questions.target: A well-designed word problem: customer growth for a small business
questions.answer: (a) $\frac{180}{240}\times100=75\%$. (b) New customers $=240\times1.25=300$. Repeat customers $=0.75\times300=225$. (c) 80\% of 300 is $0.8\times300=240$ repeat customers needed. Additional customers needed $=240-225=15$.
questions.explanation: (a) $\frac{180}{240}\times100=75\%$. (b) New customers $=240\times1.25=300$. Repeat customers $=0.75\times300=225$. (c) 80\% of 300 is $0.8\times300=240$ repeat customers needed. Additional customers needed $=240-225=15$.

questions.q: If 9 workers can complete a task in 12 days, how many days would it take 6 workers, assuming the same work rate per worker?
questions.answer: Total work $=9\times12=108$ worker-days. Days for 6 workers $=\frac{108}{6}=18$.

questions.q: A map has a scale of 1 cm to 17 km. If two cities are 15.5 cm apart on the map, find the actual distance between them.
A map has a scale of 1 cm to 11 km. If two cities are 6.5 cm apart on the map, find the actual distance between them.
The ratio of red, blue, and yellow marbles in a bag is $3:4:5$. If there are $48$ marbles in total, how many blue marbles are there?
questions.answer: Total ratio parts $= 3 + 4 + 5 = 12$. Each part $= \frac{48}{12} = 4$. Blue marbles $= 4 \times 4 = 16$.
questions.explanation: Total ratio parts $= 3 + 4 + 5 = 12$. Each part $= \frac{48}{12} = 4$. Blue marbles $= 4 \times 4 = 16$.

questions.q: A map has a scale of $1 \mathrm{\ cm} : 25 \mathrm{\ km}$. If two cities are $7.2$ cm apart on the map, what is the actual distance between them?
If $40\%$ of $x$ is equal to $30\%$ of $y$, what is the ratio $\frac{x}{y}$?

Train A leaves a station traveling east at $80$ km/h. Two hours later, Train B leaves the same station traveling east on a parallel track at $120$ km/h. How many hours after Train B departs will it overtake Train A?
questions.answer: Head start of Train A $= 80 \times 2 = 160$ km. Relative closing speed $= 120 - 80 = 40$ km/h. Time $= \frac{160}{40} = 4$ hours.
questions.explanation: Head start of Train A $= 80 \times 2 = 160$ km. Relative closing speed $= 120 - 80 = 40$ km/h. Time $= \frac{160}{40} = 4$ hours.

questions.q: In a survey of $200$ high school seniors, $120$ plan to attend college, $50$ plan to work, and $30$ are undecided. If a student is chosen at random, what is the probability that the student does NOT plan to work?
questions.answer: Students not planning to work $= 200 - 50 = 150$. Probability $= \frac{150}{200} = \frac{3}{4}$.
questions.explanation: Students not planning to work $= 200 - 50 = 150$. Probability $= \frac{150}{200} = \frac{3}{4}$.
